title: 0. Executive Thesis, Dual Verdict & Opportunity Matrix

epigraph.quote: Own the tollbooths of daily household consumption—but buy them when the tape tests support, never when the crowd bids defensive safety above twenty-one times forward earnings.
epigraph.author: Executive Underwriting Summary

web_blocks.html: The State Street Consumer Staples Select Sector SPDR ETF (XLP) is the premier institutional vehicle for U.S. consumer staples exposure. It holds $15.00 billion ($14,996.34M) in AUM, charges a 0.08% gross expense ratio, and trades with a 0.01% 30-day median spread [1, 20]. Its trailing distribution yield is 2.43% ($2.20 per share).

XLP owns 34 S&P 500 staples leaders across six industries: Distribution & Retail (34.73%), Beverages (19.77%), Household Products (18.53%), Food Products (15.28%), Tobacco (10.27%), and Personal Care (1.43%) [1]. Our refreshed Pass 1 audit awards COMPOUNDER_PASS with kpi_health: PASS_WITH_WATCH. Walmart (11.47%) and Costco (9.83%) drive 21.30% of the fund, while one-time 2026 IEEPA tariff refunds, -$2.27B in 1-year ETF outflows, and 23.5% U.S. private-label share warrant ongoing monitoring [29, 30, 32].

At the November 20, 2026 close of $90.46 (Nov 23 TradingView $90.41 / Finviz $90.57), XLP sits in a confirmed Stan Weinstein Stage 2 uptrend [25]. Price holds +5.73% above its 30-week SMA ($85.51) and +4.50% above its 50-day SMA ($86.52) in a 6.81% Bollinger squeeze, while the broader U.S. market sits in a Downtrend (38.8% breadth > 50-DMA, 10 distribution days).

At 21.20x FY1 forward P/E against a 5.04% 10-year Treasury yield, XLP's +5.51% 15-month probability-weighted total return (~4.4% annualized EV) trails risk-free Treasuries amid -$2.27B in 1-year ETF outflows. Under an 18.5x normalization stress, Base fair value drops to $85.66 and EV falls to $88.33 (below the $88.51 support shelf), while a 3.0% EPS growth haircut yields $81.96 at 18.5x and $79.74 at 18.0x. We downgrade XLP to REJECTED (TIER_0, VALUATION), decline options (NO_OPTIONS_EDGE), and maintain our upward-ratcheted $84.77 stop reference (>= $84.54 prior). XLP is NOT_HELD (0 shares), and portfolio cash sits at 9.13% ($7,290.91 of $79,861.16 NAV) vs. a 22.0% Downtrend floor, so we retain 100% of marginal cash in USD Cash/T-Bills.

book_paragraphs: Welcome to our refreshed institutional monograph on XLP, the State Street Consumer Staples Select Sector SPDR ETF. Over the next nine chapters, we examine a $15.00 billion sector vehicle that charges 0.08% a year to own 34 S&P 500 household brands and retail giants, led by Walmart (11.47%) and Costco (9.83%).

In Pass 1, we audited the business and new Q3 2026 filings completely blind to price, awarding COMPOUNDER_PASS with a PASS_WITH_WATCH flag for one-time IEEPA tariff refunds, -$2.27 billion in 1-year ETF outflows, 23.5% private-label share, and 21% household GLP-1 adoption. Only then did we open the November 20, 2026 market tape.

At $90.46, XLP holds a confirmed Stage 2 uptrend while the U.S. market sits in a Downtrend (38.8% breadth > 50-DMA, 10 distribution days), yet 21.20x forward earnings against a 5.04% 10-year Treasury delivers just +4.4% annualized expected total return—trailing risk-free Treasuries. Stress-testing the multiple to its 18.5x historical norm drops Base fair value to $85.66 and expected value to $88.33 (below the $88.51 support shelf), while a 3.0% EPS haircut yields $81.96 at 18.5x and $79.74 at 18.0x. Because XLP is NOT_HELD, options lack edge (NO_OPTIONS_EDGE / DECLINED), and portfolio cash is 9.13% versus a 22.0% Downtrend floor, our verdict is REJECTED (TIER_0, VALUATION): retain 100% of marginal capital in cash with our upward-ratcheted $84.77 stop reference intact.
